text: Cháu — if you're reading this, the fire's lit again. This book was my map; now it's yours. Fill the pages I couldn't. The forest remembers me kindly — let it remember you. — Ông
Morning! I'm Mai — ranger on this stretch. Your grandpa kept this camp thirty years. The board fills with travelers tonight; seat them well and I'll open the Outfitter. — Mai

theme: Some like company, some like quiet
text: Some like company, some like quiet. Read the cards, cháu — a Social soul beside a shy one makes a long night for both. The pads remember where you place them. — Ông
Rain's coming day after tomorrow. Canvas sheds water; campers don't. A Tarp over the pads keeps the stars — and the reviews — dry. Forecast's pinned to the board. — Mai
Nobody wants just one thing. Watch for the second wish — the quiet one. Feed it, and the fifth star follows. — Ông
Grandpa ran a drill every day — one board, no retries. Called it practice camp. The Trail Daily's on the board if you want the same reps. — Mai

theme: A full pot is a full camp
text: A full pot is a full camp. Two things in the pot, any two — the fire decides what they become. Write down what works, cháu. — Ông
A family booked! Mind the little ones — they want room to run, and the noise carries. Light Sleepers don't forgive. — Ông
Folks are talking — your rating's real. Walk-ins come for the leftovers when the word's good. More seats, more mouths, more coins. — Mai
The page turns. Further up the river there's a camp I never finished — the water there sings different. Pack light. — Ông
You found the river. Old Ba still fishes the south bank — he knew me. Feed him well. — Ông
Anglers want the bank pads — river sound does half the work. Keep the rod oiled; the fishing's honest here. — Mai
Ba told you about the koi? He never told anyone but me. The river keeps its promises, cháu — keep yours. — Ông
Your grandmother painted lanterns here once. I never said that in the letters home. Some things belong to the trail. — Ông
Word's out — the rating's real. River folk come a long way for a warm pad. — Mai
High ground next. The valley where the lanterns float — I left something burning there for you. — Ông
The chapter closes. Up the switchbacks — Lantern Valley waits. — Ông
The valley at dusk — a hundred lanterns and one that's always dark. Light it for me. — Ông
Photographers come for the south terrace. Keep the sky clear and the lights low. — Mai
Lan's exhibition — she caught the camp at golden hour. Your grandmother would have wept, then asked for prints. — Ông
I proposed here. Under the arch, before the lanterns rose. Some pages I wrote for you, cháu — some I wrote for myself. — Ông
Full houses now — eight pads, all claimed by dark. The valley rewards the ready. — Mai
Last pages, cháu. Not the end of the book — the end of this one. — Ông
There's a cove past the cape where the water stays glass. Glasscoast. When you're ready — the trail continues. — Ông
Cháu — tonight is his memorial. I'll bring the lantern; you bring the camp. If the stove can manage chè trôi nước, he'd like that — it was his offering food. No pressure. Just come. — Mai
Cháu — the committee approved the first project: a bench at the overlook. It ships with this letter. Grandpa's fund, working again after all these years. — Mai
You won't believe what the fund found in his papers — the way-marker design he carved for the east fork. We had it made. It's yours now. — Mai
The committee asked me what the fund's last project should be. I said a stone, at the head of his trail, with his name on it. It arrived today. Take care placing it — it matters. — Mai
Cháu — three days of rain means gutter season. Grandpa used to cut a channel behind pad 3. The shovel's by the shed if you want it. The guests won't mind the mud; they never do. — Mai
